raw.cause: nav_handle() sleeps 200 ms (the COCKPIT_FAULT=slow-reply branch) between receiving display's request and calling MsgReply, so display's tid 1 stays REPLY-blocked for about 200 ms on every route request. All 14 completed round trips take roughly 202-222 ms against a 50 ms budget, and the last request is still unanswered at trace end. This is a delay inside the server, not a priority problem: nav inherits display's priority while it handles the message, and its own gps and logger calls are evidently fast.
raw.qnx_call: MsgReply delayed in nav (nav_handle sleeps 200 ms before the reply, keeping display REPLY-blocked in MsgSend)
raw.fix_summary: Remove the 200 ms sleep from nav's request path so nav replies as soon as it has the gps position. If nav really needs that long to compute a route, don't do it while display waits: precompute the route periodically and reply with the cached one. Otherwise the contract's nav budget has to be raised, which would make display's frame rate depend on nav.
